question: What orientation and locator-tone requirements apply to an accessible pedestrian push button?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Each accessible pedestrian push button must have a vibrotactile arrow on the button itself, with high visual contrast, aligned parallel to the direction of travel on the associated crosswalk, so pedestrians with vision disabilities can identify the correct crosswalk and align themselves. A locator tone is required to help pedestrians find the vibrotactile arrow and push button; the tone must be deactivated during flashing operation (with a specified exception), and if audible beaconing is used, its volume during the pedestrian change interval may be raised only up to 100 dBA from a far-end loudspeaker mounted 7 to 10 feet above the pavement. Standards (mandatory): - "each push button shall clearly indicate by means of a vibrotactile arrow which crosswalk signal is actuated by the push button. Vibrotactile arrows shall be located on the button of the push button assembly, shall have high visual contrast (light on dark or dark on light), and shall be aligned parallel to the direction of travel on the associated crosswalk." - "A locator tone shall be incorporated into the accessible pedestrian signal equipment to help pedestrians with vision disabilities locate the vibrotactile arrow, and the associated push button if a push button is provided." - "Push button locator tones shall be deactivated when the traffic control signal or pedestrian hybrid beacon is operating in a flashing mode. This requirement shall not apply to traffic control signals or pedestrian hybrid beacons that are activated from a flashing or dark mode to a steady (stop-and-go) mode by pedestrian actuations." - "If audible beaconing is used, the volume of the push button locator tone during the pedestrian change interval of the called pedestrian phase shall be increased up to a maximum of 100 dBA, and shall come from a loudspeaker that is mounted at the far end of the crosswalk at a height of 7 to 10 feet above the pavement." - "At accessible pedestrian signal locations where pressing the pedestrian push button is necessary to activate the walk interval, pressing the pedestrian push button shall activate both the walk interval and the accessible pedestrian signals." - "Where used, push buttons intended to be used by both pedestrians and bicyclists shall be located and operated to meet all accessibility requirements (see Section 4I.05)." Citations: - Section 4K.04 Standard §1 (p.734) - Section 4K.04 Standard §2 (p.734) - Section 4K.04 Standard §6 (p.734) - Section 4K.05 Standard §8 (p.735) - Section 4K.01 Standard §14 (p.732) - Section 4H.12 Standard §3 (p.717)
gold_answer: The push button must have a high-contrast vibrotactile arrow on the button, aligned parallel to travel on the associated crosswalk. A locator tone must be incorporated; normally it is 0.15 seconds or less and repeats at 1-second intervals when the audible walk indication is not active, subject to stated exceptions.
